A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same amortized Bayesian workflow. All 9 pages of v1 and 26 pages of v2, including their appendices, are readable, and corresponding text, equations, tables, and figures can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original GEV simulation results, workflow acceptance counts and runtimes, posterior calibration and recovery diagnostics, and a ChEES-HMC initialization experiment.

after.justification: v2 reports original workflow evaluations on four problems, including analyses of mouse behavioral and human decision datasets, together with calibration diagnostics and ChEES-HMC and NUTS initialization experiments.

M1.justification: The three-stage workflow is retained, but its first-stage acceptance procedure changes from an MMD-based atypicality test to Mahalanobis distance in summary space. The implemented posterior estimator also changes from flow matching to a six-layer coupling-based normalizing flow, with the GEV summary representation increasing from 8 to 16 dimensions. These change the actual inference implementation.

E1.justification: v2 retains the GEV problem and adds Bernoulli GLM inference on 10,000 synthetic datasets, psychometric inference on 8,526 mouse behavioral datasets, and drift-diffusion inference for 15,000 human participants. The GEV prior equations and 65-observation task remain unchanged; v2 clarifies that twice the prior width means four times the variance.

E2.justification: The principal runtime comparison changes from an estimated NUTS-HMC run over all datasets in v1 to an estimated ChEES-HMC run over all datasets in v2 Table 1. This substantially revises the efficiency benchmark. The three initialization comparators—raw amortized draws, PSIS-refined draws, and random initialization—are retained.

E3.justification: Posterior-quality evaluation changes from MMD to 1-Wasserstein and mean marginal total variation distances, with v2 specifying evaluation on up to 100 datasets per inference step. Reported training settings change from Adam to AdamW, with revised learning rates and gradient clipping. Runtime hardware changes from A100 to V100. Appendix D adds a NUTS warmup evaluation using R-hat; the existing 2048-chain, 200-warmup-step ChEES-HMC configuration remains.

E4.justification: The GEV initialization analysis is revised and extended across all four problems in v2 Figure 6. Appendix D adds the corresponding NUTS analysis. Figure 5 newly separates accepted and rejected amortized draws to examine diagnostic effectiveness, while Figures 8–10 add parameter-recovery and calibration analyses for the additional problems.

E5.justification: v1 Table 1 reports posterior discrepancies as medians with 95% confidence intervals; v2 replaces these summaries with W1/MMTV boxplots. Median-plus-IQR summaries across 20 datasets and SBC 95% confidence bands are retained. Neither version reports repeated-training-run counts or random seeds.

E6.justification: GEV acceptance counts change from 678, 228, and 66 across the three steps to 523, 357, and 87, changing total acceptance from 972/1000 to 967/1000. Reported total runtime changes from 664 seconds to 15 minutes. These are replacement results under changed methods and hardware, not same-setting performance changes. v2 also adds results for three other problems and reports task-dependent initialization benefits, including occasional worsening from PSIS refinement.

T1.justification: The formal OOD discrepancy and rejection rule change from MMD to Mahalanobis distance in v2 Equations 8–9. v2 adds probabilistic-model and Pareto-tail definitions, while dropping v1's explicit NRMSE and interval-coverage equations. These are localized formal changes without new proofs or accuracy guarantees. The added Equation 7 contains a sign error in its k=0 exponential branch.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that diagnostic-guided escalation from amortized inference through PSIS to MCMC, while reusing posterior draws, combines speed and posterior accuracy across many datasets. v2's new abstract and broader demonstrations preserve this central contribution; the additional supporting evidence does not redefine it.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive limitations concerning upfront training costs, high-dimensional or weakly identifiable models, and acceptance of poor amortized draws by the OOD diagnostic. It qualifies PSIS usefulness to low or moderate dimensions and discusses alternative diagnostics and sampler choices. The initialization interpretation also changes: v1 emphasizes improved worst-case behavior from PSIS, whereas v2 acknowledges occasional degradation and task-dependent benefits.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands architecture, optimization, validation-checkpoint, simulation-budget, hardware, software, and parameter-transformation documentation. It adds real-data retrieval and tensor-format instructions and states that reproduction code accompanies the supplementary material. However, v1's explicit fallback when PSIS cannot supply enough unique initialization draws and its ChEES-HMC initial step size are omitted.

R1.justification: The new Related Work section substantially expands positioning relative to neural posterior corrections, flow-assisted MCMC, transport preconditioning, and initialization methods such as Pathfinder. Additional discussion connects the diagnostic choices to posterior SBC and L-C2ST. This extends well beyond updates to existing references such as the PSIS publication.

P1.justification: v2 develops the extended abstract into a full narrative with a new abstract, substantially expanded introduction and method explanations, separate experimental procedure and application subsections, and a detailed Discussion. The appendices are reorganized into background, diagnostics, experiment details, and NUTS analysis. Author ordering and affiliation text also change.

P2.justification: Table 1 becomes a four-problem runtime comparison, and posterior-quality distributions move into new boxplots. The atypicality plot is revised and moved from the appendix to the main text; the initialization plot expands to four panels. New calibration and NUTS figures accompany the retained workflow illustrations. Figure 11's caption incorrectly names ChEES-HMC despite describing a NUTS experiment.

improvement.justification: v1 supports the workflow with one synthetic GEV demonstration. v2 substantially strengthens practical validation through four problems, including two large real-data applications, a parallel-MCMC runtime comparator, and analyses showing when initialization benefits fail to generalize. Expanded reproducibility information and explicit diagnostic limitations improve transparency. These gains outweigh localized defects in Equation 7 and Figure 11's caption and the omission of some initialization details; changed settings do not establish a direct performance improvement.
